_parser_fn_note: CS2 is the first profile that needs more than one config file to read: resolution/screen_mode/vsync/upscaling live in cs2_video.txt, but frame_limit (fps_max) only lives in a separate machine/user convars file. The legacy _parse_cs2(all_configs) already takes the whole config-file list for this reason, so this profile sets parse_mode='multi_file' (new P1 plumbing - see Profile.parse_multi in profiles/loader.py) instead of the single-file 'main' content path the other profiles use. Writing only ever touches cs2_video.txt, so writer_fn still uses the normal single-file path - no change needed there. parser_fn/writer_fn wrap settings_parser._parse_cs2 / settings_writer._write_cs2_video verbatim (config_manager/profile_functions.py), so this migration is zero-behavior-change, INCLUDING a pre-existing quirk: the parser reads vsync from 'setting.mat_vsync' but the writer patches 'setting.mat_vsync_mode' (a real key-name mismatch in the legacy code, left as-is rather than silently fixed during migration).
_verified_note: No local runner/rules verified-games rule file or .9 run evidence exists in this checkout for Counter-Strike 2 (same caveat as the other migrated profiles) - left empty rather than fabricated.

anticheat.basis: Counter-Strike 2 ships Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC), but VAC is NOT in config_manager/anticheat.py's vendor/detection tables (only EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, EA Javelin, nProtect GameGuard, XIGNCODE3, Anti-Cheat Expert, PunkBuster, mhyprot are known there) - detect_anticheat() will currently return nothing for this title even though real anti-cheat is present. Add a VAC entry to anticheat.py and re-scan a real install before treating writes as broadly safe.
